Hello everyone, I felt like I wanted to write a bit about the current situation over at reddit and share with you my thoughts on this matter. I try to structure this using some statements that you may agree or disagree with. Please, if you have any opinions about them, by all means voice them :) Also, a lot of the things I am listing here have been said somewhere else, but I have not seen a post that consolidated these ideas.

Reddit needs to drastically change in order to be profitable

In 2013, Reddit was still unprovitable, in 2014 Reddit only made 8.3M in ad revenue that would mean that along with other revenue streams, this is still not enough to cover its expenses. Now I am not an economist (please chime in if you are), but even if that figure would be profit, it would still take 6 years to get any kind of return on investment (ROI) for the 50M capital they got. Because this isn't, they probably need to make more profit in the future than their entire revenue steam in the past!

So, in order to do this, these current plans are put in motion. Pao and crew need to quickly monetize and thus change the entire business completely; they have about 20M of annual revenue to deliver to the stakeholders!

Pao is not the problem

A lot of posts have been primarily anti Pao (and why not, she seems to be a really unlikable person), but these restructurings are part of the problem mentioned above. Reddit as a company is cutting away the unprofitable parts (hosting of discussions, expression, etc), is changing the okay parts (AMA), is investing in the profitable parts (clickbait and meme's) and gets rid of the ugly (controversial opinions, later nsfw material)

For Pao and perhaps others the only job they have is to take the blame, change the business and get out of there.

One thing I am not so certain about is how well they thought this through. One might say; 'not at all, look at how Victoria got fired!' But I want to argue against that, for their purposes, it is a lot better to have a team of marketeers and PR doing that job than someone who is passionate in being the person who connects everything. After all, the former know how to bring in money.

Communities will shatter

It is clear that the reddit now will look vastly different in a year. My prediction is that as a company it will do okay - not great, but it will also not tank. It will be a site where younger people go for their meme's, semi curated news and opinions. AMA will be changed to accommodate that, no really controversial guests, maybe 'controversial' celebrities.

Voat (if nothing else comes along in its growth phase) will be the home for more insight full conversations, and will mostly look like reddit a couple of years back. People do share meme's and in-jokes, but in a more pleasant way.

Controversial topics will not be completely banned from Reddit, although a couple of mini meltdowns let everyone know they are not welcome over there. Some come to Voat, others flee to *chan or other outlets.
A prediction for the future of Reddit and Voat.

Their biggest problem is that there is not a lot of precedent for monetizing something like Reddit. There are no experts, and very few good examples to follow. Digg's down fall was caused by the exact same need to monetize, they just made different mistakes.

It's not just that they are greedy, money hungry and out to make a quick buck. People have invested serious cash in Reddit and management is obligated to show a return.

This whole Victoria thing was a direct result of them trying to monetize AMAs. The FPH banning was part of their attempt to clean up their image for advertisers.

Reddit is going to keep making changes. Those changes are mostly going to be shots in the dark and most of them are going to tick off users. They are just hoping that some of those changes can successfully make lots of money before they lose a critical mass of users (a la Digg).

It seems to me the best way to monetize would be selling user info to companies like google. If they could tie an account to a real identity, the list of subreddits they are subscribed to, and their comments(if they could be easily datamined) would provide a great picture of their interests and be worth a lot of money to ad companies.

Now doing this would probably piss off a significant part of the userbase, but at this point they dont seem to care.

And even if they managed to do that (say, using an user's IP address to identify them) there would need the trouble of the rest of reddit figuring out about it.

I imagine that would trigger an even bigger flood of users from reddit to alternatives, mainly voat.
